name: Obernberger See
kurzbeschreibung: Obernberger See at 1,590 m in the Wipptal: emerald-green natural gem at the foot of the Tribulaun, featuring the baroque Seekapelle Maria am See on a peninsula.
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Obernberger See lies at an elevation of 1,590 metres above sea level at the idyllic head of the Obernbergtal, a pristine side valley of the Tyrolean Wipptal near the Brenner Pass. Nestled within a strictly protected landscape conservation area and towered over by the rugged limestone crags of the imposing Obernberger Tribulaun (2,780 m), this crystal-clear mountain lake is regarded as one of Tyrol's most enchanting and photogenic natural monuments. With its glowing shades of emerald and turquoise, ancient larch forests, and the idyllic lake chapel enthroned on a promontory, the area magnetically draws nature lovers and mountain hikers in every season.

Geology, Seekapelle & Natural Haven

The origin of the lake traces back to a dramatic post-glacial natural event: thousands of years ago, gigantic rock masses broke loose from the flanks of the Tribulaun and crashed into the valley. This prehistoric Bergsturz (rockslide) dammed the mountain streams and shaped an undulating landscape of mounds that today divides the lake into a shallower Vordersee and a deeper Hintersee. At normal water levels, both basins are joined; the lake covers roughly 16 hectares and reaches depths of up to 15 metres. Fed exclusively by subterranean karst springs, its waters boast pristine drinking quality. The cultural and historical centrepiece is the baroque chapel Seekapelle Maria am See: erected in 1732 on a wooded island or peninsula, the whitewashed chapel is connected to the shore via a picturesque wooden bridge. Inside, it shelters an exquisitely crafted baroque Marian altar. To permanently safeguard the sensitive ecological equilibrium, rare stonewort algae, and abundant stocks of Arctic char and trout, a strict swimming ban applies to both humans and dogs across the entire lake, alongside a ban on boats and stand-up paddleboards.

Visit & Getting There

The lake and the entire protected landscape area are freely open to visitors year-round and free of charge. A leisurely circular trail of around 5.5 kilometres leads completely around the lake (walking time approx. 1.5 to 2 hours). Arrival by car: via the Brennerautobahn A13 (exit Nösslach or Matrei) or toll-free along the Brenner federal road B182 to Gries am Brenner; turn into the Obernbergtal and follow state road L38 to the valley head to reach the large paid hiking car park Waldesruh (daily fee approx. €5.00). From the car park, a comfortable and wide forest track gently climbs to the lake shore in about 35 to 45 minutes. By public transport: take the ÖBB S-Bahn (S3) to Steinach am Brenner or Gries am Brenner station, where VVT bus line 4145 runs regularly straight to the terminus Obernberg Waldesruh.

Tips

The wide forest track from the Waldesruh car park to the lakeshore and the path along the western shore are solidly surfaced and ideal for all-terrain pushchairs; the steeper forest path on the eastern bank requires sturdy hiking boots. For refreshments, visit Almgasthof Waldesruh at the car park or Almis Berghotel in the village. In late autumn, when the surrounding larch forests turn vibrant golden-yellow and the snow-dusted crags of the Tribulaun are mirrored in the mirror-like waters, visitors can experience one of the most magnificent natural spectacles in the entire Alps.
